title: ProjectE benchmark and pass-rate report
description: Output of tools/scripts/benchmark.py. The three axes - outcome, determinism, coverage - are kept separate on purpose and are never collapsed into a single headline number. 'scope' is required and pinned to tool_invocations so a tool-level pass rate cannot be read as an end-to-end agent success rate; the agent's tool CHOICE is the stochastic part of this system and this harness does not exercise it.

scope.description: Pinned. This measures declared argv invocations of individual tools, not the agent choosing them. Widening the scope must be a schema revision, not a quiet relabelling of the same number.

status.description: GREEN requires that every problem in the set was actually measured: ANY uncovered problem (missing tool, absent dependency) makes this NO_COVERAGE. It used to say NO_COVERAGE only when EVERY problem was uncovered, so losing one tool out of twenty still read GREEN.

items.description: NOTHING_COVERED = the harness measured nothing at all. PROBLEM_UNCOVERED = it measured part of the set and lost the rest; summary.uncovered_ids names them.

repetitions.description: At least 2: a single run cannot detect nondeterminism, which is the property this harness exists to measure.

determinism_unknown.description: Problems whose tool printed no JSON report, so there was nothing to compare between runs. UNKNOWN is a third state, distinct from nondeterministic: collapsing the two flagged 20 well-behaved self-tests as defective on the first real run.

problem_pass_rate.description: Fraction of COVERED problems that passed every repetition. Null when nothing was covered - not 0, which would read as total failure.

reason_codes.description: Histogram of the reason codes the tools themselves emitted. This is the root-cause view: a failing problem says WHY it failed in the tool's own vocabulary.

heat_map.description: The compact per-problem view: passed-of-covered plus the determinism flag. Structured rows rather than rendered characters, so a consumer can sort and filter it.

expect.description: RED and ERROR entries are the fault injections: a problem set of only happy paths cannot tell a working gate from one wired to always pass.

deterministic.description: null means UNKNOWN - the tool emitted no JSON to compare.
